title: Normalized finite-coefficient Kummer generator
statement: For a finite commutative ring A killed by ell^N, N>=1, and algebraically closed Omega with ell invertible, the coefficient Kummer class kappa_A(t) of [def-pur-rank-one-local-data] is an A-basis of the ordinary degree-one cohomology of the punctured affine line. Equivalently there is an A-module isomorphism A to that derived evaluation group sending 1 to kappa_A(t). The coefficient map is characterized by z mapping to 1 tensor z. This includes the zero ring.

proof.text: Choose a primitive root to trivialize the root line. The adopted source AffineLineKummer proves the finite-abelian-coefficient Kummer calculation: pushing forward the coordinate root class identifies Hom(Z/m,A) with H1 of the constant A sheaf, by finite abelian group decomposition. Hence this cohomology has the finite cardinality of A. The proved adopted-source APIs are AlgebraicGeometry.AffineSpace.bijective_sheafHConstantSheafNatTrans, subsingleton_sheafH_constantSheaf_line, and subsingleton_sheafH_constantSheaf_multiplicativeGroup in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Curve.AffineLineKummer; no new unproved assertion is used.

Use exact restriction and the represented-section unit to identify Ext of the open object with global cohomology on the punctured line. MapExtPrecomp is bijective, and its composition laws plus Kummer-sequence restriction show that the displayed extension class maps to the usual Kummer boundary of t. Maps between constant abelian sheaves restrict surjectively, by fullness of the constant-sheaf functor on the connected open. Hence every degree-one class is the displayed coefficient Kummer class for a root coefficient map on the affine line. The explicit tensor/sheafification adjunction factors this map through the given z to 1 tensor z insertion and an endomorphism of the finite twist. The proved source rank-one constant-sheaf endomorphism lemma makes it a scalar. Naturality of the forward module/Ext comparison and scalar compatibility of derived evaluation give a scalar multiple of the given kappa(t). Thus a to a kappa(t) is surjective; equal finite cardinalities give bijectivity. Its linear equivalence sends 1 exactly to kappa(t).

lean.statement:
theorem finite_kummer_generator
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (ℓ N : ℕ) (_hℓ : ℓ.Prime) (hℓΩ : IsUnit (ℓ : Ω)) (_hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (hA : ((ℓ ^ N : ℕ) : A) = 0)
    (hm : IsUnit ((ℓ ^ N : ℕ) : Γ(Line (Spec (.of Ω)), ⊤)))
    (f : (Line (Spec (.of Ω))).rootsOfUnitySheaf (ℓ ^ N) ⟶
      (Etale.moduleAbelianForget A (Line (Spec (.of Ω)))).obj
        (Scheme.finiteEtaleTateSheaf A (ℓ ^ N) (Line (Spec (.of Ω))) hA 1))
    (hf : ∀ V z, f.hom.app V z =
      Scheme.finiteEtaleTateOneGenerator A (ℓ ^ N) (Line (Spec (.of Ω))) hA V 1 z) :
    let X := Line (Spec (.of Ω))
    let F := Scheme.finiteEtaleTateSheaf A (ℓ ^ N) X hA 1
    let κ := kummerClass A X (openObject (Spec (.of Ω))) F (ℓ ^ N) hm f
    (∃ τ : ModuleCat.of A A ≅
        ((sections X.smallEtaleTopology A (openObject (Spec (.of Ω)))).rightDerived 1).obj F,
      τ.hom 1 = κ (coordinateUnit (Spec (.of Ω))))
